rows: Why is limestone parent material more fertile than granite?
Limestone weathers to Ca2+, Mg2+, HCO3-; maintains high pH; higher CEC; granite releases K+ but is acidic and coarse
Why are tropical soils often nutrient-poor?
Highly weathered (millions of yr); all primary minerals consumed; only Fe/Al oxides and kaolinite remain; nutrients held in biomass, not mineral soil
Why are loess-derived soils (Mollisols) so fertile?
Fine silt particle size + carbonate minerals + grassland OM accumulation = high CEC + high SOM + favorable pH
What drives podzol (spodosol) formation under boreal conifers?
Acidic conifer litter + chelating organic acids mobilize Fe/Al from E horizon → Bhs accumulation
What chemical weathering reaction drives the long-term carbon cycle?
Silicate hydrolysis consumes CO2 to form bicarbonate; transported to ocean; precipitated as CaCO3 over millions of years
How fast do soils form vs. how fast do they erode under cultivation?
Formation: ~0.01–0.1 mm/yr; erosion under cultivation: 1–10 mm/yr → net loss in most row-crop agriculture
